skill.title: Interpret operations as transformations on the Argand diagram
needs: Plot complex numbers on an Argand diagram

lines.text: The conjugate changes the sign of the imaginary part.
$iu = -b + ai$ is the point $(-b, a)$: left of the imaginary axis and a small height above the real axis.
$\overline{iu} = -b - ai$ is the point $(-b, -a)$, the reflection of $iu$ in the real axis.

steps.title: (iii) Describe a transformation from u to the conjugate of iu

lines.text: Multiplying by $i$ turns $u$ into $iu$: a rotation of $90^\circ$ anticlockwise about the origin.
Then reflecting $iu$ in the real axis gives $\overline{iu}$.

references.final: iu = -b + ai,\ \overline{iu} = -b - ai;\ \text{rotate } 90^\circ \text{ anticlockwise about the origin, then reflect in the real axis}

lines.text: The conjugate changes the sign of the imaginary part.
$1 - 2i$ has the same real part as $w$ and lies the same distance below the real axis, so it is $w$ reflected in the real axis. That is point $C$.

references.final: \text{Box } C \text{ (the conjugate is the reflection of } w \text{ in the real axis)}
